newsitem.title: FINLAND: SILJA SAYS SWEDISH FLAG TO HELP MARKETING.
newsitem.headline: SILJA SAYS SWEDISH FLAG TO HELP MARKETING.

text.p: Finnish passenger ferry operator Silja Oy said on Thursday the intention in moving its Festival ferry to Sweden's ship register from sailing under Finnish flag is to promote marketing in Sweden.
"The flag has an impact on marketing. It is a question of the company's image," Silja vice president corporate communications Eeva Korhonen told Reuters by telephone.
The transport ministry said earlier the government had allowed Silja to transfer Silja Festival to Sweden's ship register.
Korhonen said Silja wants to have ferries flying both Finland's and Sweden's flags to stress its tradition as a company operating in both countries.
From April, five of Silja's Silja Line ferries between Finland and Sweden will fly the Finnish flag and three vessels the Swedish one.
Festival -- currently operating between Helsinki and Estonia's Tallinn -- will replace Silja Scandinavia on the Turku-Stockholm route in April 1997.
Silja's main competitor Viking Line announced on November 18 it had purchased Silja Scandinavia from the Swedish company which had been leasing it to Silja.
Korhonen said Silja has no immediate needs to increase its capacity after Scandinavia's leasing agreement expires.
"We don't, not at least during winter months," she said, when asked whether Silja planed to increase its tonnage.
Silja will maintain its capacity between Helsinki and Tallinn by increasing the pace of the one remaining ship, Korhonen said.
She said Silja already last summer decided not to use its option to extend Scandinavia's leasing agreement, which was due to expire by April 1997.
